problem: The blanket statement 'onSaveInstanceState runs after onPause and before onStop' is only true for apps targeting below Android 9 (API 28). For apps targeting API 28 or higher the system calls it after onStop, so a student who memorises this sentence will be wrong for modern targetSdk values.
fix: Write: 'onSaveInstanceState(outState) runs after onPause. For apps targeting Android 9 (API 28) or higher it runs after onStop; on older targets it runs between onPause and onStop. In every case it runs while the activity is being stopped, before the process may be killed, and it is skipped when the activity is finishing for good.'

problem: 'onPause or onSaveInstanceState, which always run before the activity can be hidden or killed' overstates both callbacks. onSaveInstanceState is not called at all when the user presses Back (the activity is finishing), and on new targets it runs after the activity is already hidden (after onStop).
fix: 'onPause always runs before the activity is hidden, so save there. onSaveInstanceState also runs before the activity may be killed for a configuration change or process death, but it is skipped when the activity is finishing, such as on a Back press.'

problem: Step (d) ends with onDestroy, so the activity no longer exists. Step (e) then says 'rotate while the activity is resumed', which is only possible after a fresh launch. The total of 17 treats (a) to (e) as one continuous session, but a real session would log 3 more lines (onCreate, onStart, onResume) before the rotation.
fix: Say either: '(e) is a separate run of the app: relaunch it first, which adds onCreate, onStart, onResume, so the rotation sequence is the last 6 of 9 lines and the grand total is 20', or keep 17 but state clearly that (a) to (e) are independent scenarios, not one continuous session.
